# viridisSYR

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.path = "man/figures/README-",
                      dev = "png", dpi = 150, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 1.2)
pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
```

An R package with one continuous colour scale in the [viridis](https://sjmgarnier.github.io/viridis/) family,
anchored to Syracuse University colours. **viridisSYR** starts at Syracuse navy (`#000E54`), passes through the
viridis *plasma* start colour (`#0D0887`) and purple (`#7E03A8`) and then Syracuse orange (`#F76700`), and ends at the
plasma yellow (`#F0F921`).

```{r bar, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7.2, fig.height = 4.1}
x <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 512)
cols <- syr_at(x)
pl_cols <- substr(viridisLite::plasma(512), 1, 7)               # original viridis plasma
gray_of <- function(cols) grDevices::gray(cam02ucs(cols)$Jp / 100)
h_big <- 0.6; h_sm <- 0.3                                        # the three small bars share one height
bars <- rbind(
  data.frame(x = x, y = 2.0,  h = h_big, fill = cols),                 # viridisSYR (big)
  data.frame(x = x, y = 1.38, h = h_sm,  fill = gray_of(cols)),        # viridisSYR, grayscale
  data.frame(x = x, y = 0.95, h = h_sm,  fill = pl_cols),              # viridis plasma
  data.frame(x = x, y = 0.52, h = h_sm,  fill = gray_of(pl_cols)))     # viridis plasma, grayscale
top <- 2.3                                           # top edge of the big bar
pk  <- syr_plasma_keys()                             # plasma key colours and where they sit on the scale
pl_lab <- data.frame(x = pk$closest_position, hex = pk$plasma_hex,
                     txt = paste0(pk$plasma_hex, "\n(plasma ", c("0", "25", "50", "75", "100"), "%)"))
su_lab <- data.frame(x = c(0, syr_keys()$position[4]), txt = c("#000E54\nSU navy", "#F76700\nSU orange"))
stem <- function(d, y_top) data.frame(x = d$x, y = y_top, yend = top + 0.02)
row_lab <- data.frame(y = c(2.0, 1.38, 0.95, 0.52),
                      txt = c("viridisSYR", "grayscale", "viridis plasma", "grayscale"))
ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = bars, aes(x, y, fill = fill, height = h), width = 1 / 512 * 1.05) + scale_fill_identity() +
  geom_segment(data = stem(pl_lab, top + 0.45), aes(x = x, xend = x, y = y, yend = yend),
               arrow = arrow(length = grid::unit(1.8, "mm"), type = "closed"), linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey20") +
  geom_text(data = pl_lab, aes(x, top + 0.5, label = txt), vjust = 0, size = 2.7, lineheight = 0.95) +
  geom_segment(data = stem(su_lab, top + 1.2), aes(x = x, xend = x, y = y, yend = yend),
               arrow = arrow(length = grid::unit(1.8, "mm"), type = "closed"), linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey20") +
  geom_text(data = su_lab, aes(x, top + 1.25, label = txt), vjust = 0, size = 2.9, fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.95) +
  geom_text(data = row_lab, aes(x = -0.02, y = y, label = txt), hjust = 1, size = 2.8, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.2, 1.1), breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.25, 3.9), breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "position on the scale",  y = NULL,
       caption = paste0("Top bar: viridisSYR, with the Syracuse colours (bold) and the viridis plasma key colours at the position of the same or closest colour.\n",
                        "Below: grayscale of viridisSYR (perceptual lightness J' in CAM02-UCS), original viridis plasma, and its grayscale.")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 7.5, colour = "grey30"))
```

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Syracuse University. The two Syracuse hex codes are used as published brand colours.

## Install

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("nrgslp/viridisSYR")
```

## Use

```{r use}
library(viridisSYR)

syr(5)                   # n colours, like viridisLite::viridis()
syr_keys()               # the four defining colours and their positions
syr_su()                 # the Syracuse colours, taken from the scale
syr_at(0.689)            # the colour at any position from 0 to 1
syr_value_at("su_orange", limits = c(0, 100))   # data value drawn in Syracuse orange
```

In ggplot2:

```r
ggplot(d, aes(x, y, fill = z)) + geom_raster() + scale_fill_syr_c()     # also scale_colour_syr_c()
ggplot(d, aes(x, y, colour = g)) + geom_point() + scale_colour_syr_d()  # discrete
```

The colours closest to the plasma key colours, and the code that returns them:

```{r plasmakeys}
syr_plasma_keys()[, c("plasma_position", "plasma_hex", "closest_hex", "closest_dE", "call")]
```

## Compared with plasma

`syr_compare()` evaluates the scale with the criteria used to design viridis (Smith & van der Walt, 2015):
perceptual uniformity and lightness order in CAM02-UCS, and behaviour under colour-vision-deficiency simulation.

```{r compare}
cmp <- syr_compare(deficiency = "none")
cmp[, c("scale", "J_start", "J_end", "J_monotone", "J_r2", "dE_cv", "chroma_mean")]
```

SYR keeps plasma's lightness order and colour sequence but is less uniform than plasma (`dE_cv` is the
coefficient of variation of the colour difference between neighbouring colours; lower is more uniform), because it
is bent through two fixed colours. See `vignette("compare-with-plasma")` for the full comparison, and
`vignette("viridisSYR")` for use cases with toy data.

## How the colours are defined

The scale is a fixed 2001-colour map (`syr.map`). It is the plasma map with two changes made in OKLab: a short lead-in from
Syracuse navy to plasma's own start colour (positions 0 to 0.05, with plasma compressed into 0.05 to 1), and a smooth offset
centred at 0.689 (where plasma is closest to Syracuse orange) that makes the scale pass exactly through `#F76700`.
`syr_build()` regenerates the map; `data-raw/syr.map.R` writes it.

## References

- Garnier, S., Ross, N., Rudis, R., Camargo, P. A., Sciaini, M., & Scherer, C. (2024). *viridis(Lite): Colorblind-friendly color maps for R.*
- Luo, M. R., Cui, G., & Li, C. (2006). Uniform colour spaces based on the CIECAM02 colour appearance model. *Color Research & Application, 31*(4), 320-330.
- Machado, G. M., Oliveira, M. M., & Fernandes, L. A. F. (2009). A physiologically-based model for simulation of color vision deficiency. *IEEE TVCG, 15*(6), 1291-1298.
- Ottosson, B. (2020). *A perceptual color space for image processing.* https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/
- Smith, N., & van der Walt, S. (2015). *A better default colormap for Matplotlib.* SciPy 2015.
